mn29:2.14: In the same way, mendicants, take the case of a gentleman who has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness, thinking,
mn29:2.15: ‘I’m swamped by rebirth, old age, and death; by sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. I’m swamped by suffering, mired in suffering.
mn29:2.16: Hopefully I can make an end to this entire mass of suffering.’
mn29:2.17: When they’ve gone forth they generate possessions, honor, and popularity.
mn29:2.18: They’re happy with that, and they’ve got all they wished for.
mn29:2.19: And they glorify themselves and put others down because of that: ‘I’m the one with possessions, honor, and popularity. These other mendicants are obscure and insignificant.’
mn29:2.20: And so they become indulgent and fall into negligence on account of those possessions, honor, and popularity. And being negligent they live in suffering.
